name: Banner Drive
narrative: Where the adventure begins… Formally elevated pallet tee box. Lots of festivity behind you. Lots of potential glory in front of you. Relatively flat fairway. Slightly breaks left. Need to be wary of the actual banner streaking diagonally across. Can be a difficult range to calibrate to off the bat with pre-round nerves. A fairly long distance to pin but very easy, especially with the dry October conditions, to blow by it. You're off n runnin!

name: Dick Basket
narrative: The lovable enigma. The Dick Basket. Any asshole can throw a dick at a basket. But can he get it to STICK??? So many approach angle options, but everyone's got a strategy until they get hit in the face with a DICK. Despite all of the above, this is still a fan favorite! Nothing captures the drama and suspense of the BBGC better than a ball teetering on the rim of the DB. Enjoy

name: Slippery Slope
narrative: Okay, again, I ask for your understanding and grace with the imperfections of this course this year after having multiple tractors and semi-trucks drive through and rip up my lawn in the process of tearing out our septic tank earlier this summer. Slippery Slope is one of the fairways impacted, at least visually, as your target landing zone wouldn't likely be before the tire treads anyway. As the name implies, this one gets SLICK, especially as the day progresses and the track gets smoothed out. One of the longer drives, but because it's downhill, muscle isn't the requirement, touch is.

name: Up N At Em
narrative: We serve Spunky Dunker Donuts and McD's breakfast sammies so you'll have the strength to drive this uphill beast. Due to the aforementioned septic truck tire treads, if you overshoot the green this year, those tread tracks serve as an escape hatch sending your ball back to you. There are rails along the right and back side of the fairway to play off of, but not advised. The best fairway at golden hour. Soak it in.

name: Bump N Run
narrative: A PHYSICAL par 3. Early shots need touch to avoid the stump gates and nestle by the pin, but second shots can get outright violent to knock balls off/near the flag. We added border logs in the rough off both sides of the green to make ball collection of errant throws easier.

name: The Vice
narrative: Gets its name from the V-shaped fairway. You can play the slope either way. Most play right to left, but you can get caught up there, or, more often, come down from right slope with too much speed and overshoot pin. The central “valley floor” of it can play really fast with drier conditions. A little tricky to gauge speed as it starts uphill but finishes w a downslope. Bottom of the pin is blind from the tee box so it gets dramatic to find out where shots wind up after all balls thrown. There is more of a backstop with an expanded flower garden bed around the electrical boxes but that area is barely within 10'.

name: Heartbreak Ridge
narrative: As the name implies, you can have a nice soft approach, but it will break your heart if it doesn't end with a release down the hard dogleg left slope to the pin. Some put balls there intentionally for defensive purposes. In recent years with more branch clearing above, some have gone the over plop route. Others, even more recently, have attempted to approach from the left, using the tree mound BEHIND the pin….if you're a back door man.

name: The Island
narrative: Yes, we have moved The Island tee box about 20ft to the left. This was done for two reasons; first of all, it eliminates the tight proximity the former tee box had with Heartbreak Ridge's green. There were some close calls of guys standing within 10ft of that pin in the queue to drive 9 and interfering with live balls. Secondly, it provides a longer landing runway AND a fun backstop. Visually more attractive as well.
